issues.description: Accessing p["fetch_date"] on a paper dict, but pipeline/fetcher.py builds each paper dict with the key "date" (fetcher.py line 33), not "fetch_date". This will raise KeyError at runtime for every fetched paper.
issues.proposed_fix: Change p["fetch_date"] to p["date"] in the INSERT VALUES tuple on run_pipeline.py line 89, or rename the key in pipeline/fetcher.py line 33 from "date" to "fetch_date" to match the database column and downstream access.

issues.description: ORDER BY confidence DESC sorts the TEXT column lexicographically, producing the order MEDIUM, LOW, HIGH instead of the intended HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW. As a result, the digest's main section lists MEDIUM-confidence papers before HIGH-confidence ones, and rows are not ranked by true confidence priority.
issues.proposed_fix: Replace the ORDER BY clause with an explicit ranking, e.g. `ORDER BY CASE confidence WHEN 'HIGH' THEN 0 WHEN 'MEDIUM' THEN 1 WHEN 'LOW' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END, title ASC`.

issues.description: `timedelta` is imported from datetime but never referenced anywhere in pipeline/fetcher.py; only `date` is used.
issues.proposed_fix: Change the import on line 2 from `from datetime import date, timedelta` to `from datetime import date`.

issues.description: The `buckets[conf]["tp"]` counter is incremented on line 83 but never read afterwards; the precision computation on lines 90-97 recomputes tp_c and relevant_predicted from `results` directly, so the tp accumulation in `buckets` is write-only.
issues.proposed_fix: Remove the if/elif block on lines 82-85 (the tp counter is unused) and keep only the `total` increment on line 81; alternatively, refactor compute_metrics to read tp/total from `buckets` instead of recomputing from results.

issues.description: The `elif r["predicted"] == "RELEVANT":` branch on lines 84-85 contains only `pass` with a comment; it is reachable but performs no work and can be removed without changing behavior.
issues.proposed_fix: Remove lines 84-85 (the elif branch with the pass statement).
